name: Yaoundé
description: Cameroon's hilly capital, often called the "City of Seven Hills." Home to the National Museum, the Reunification Monument, and the seat of government, with a cooler climate than coastal Douala.

name: Douala
description: Cameroon's largest city and economic capital, sitting on the Wouri River. The country's main port and business hub, with a lively nightlife and a fast, humid coastal energy.

name: Limbe
description: A laid-back coastal town known for its black volcanic-sand beaches, the Limbe Wildlife Centre (a primate rescue sanctuary), and views across the water to Mount Cameroon.

name: Kribi
description: A fishing town on the Atlantic coast famous for its white-sand beaches and the Lobé Waterfalls, one of the few places in the world where a waterfall empties directly into the sea.

name: Foumban
description: Historic capital of the Bamoun Kingdom. Its Royal Palace and Museum house centuries of Bamoun art, manuscripts, and royal artifacts, and the town remains a center for traditional bronze and craft work.

name: Dschang
description: A highland town known for its unusually cool, misty climate for Cameroon. Home to the University of Dschang and a well-known artisanal market showcasing regional craftsmanship.

name: Buea
description: Sitting at the foot of Mount Cameroon, West Africa's highest peak and an active volcano. Once the capital of German Kamerun, and now the starting point for the annual "Race of Hope" up the mountain.

name: Bamenda
description: A hill city built across dramatic escarpments, and the gateway to the scenic "Ring Road" — a loop through highland villages, waterfalls, and traditional Grassfields chieftaincies.

name: Rhumsiki
description: A remote village in the Mandara Mountains, known for the dramatic volcanic-plug peak that towers over it. Home to the Kapsiki people and their traditional crab-divination practice.

name: Waza National Park
description: Cameroon's premier savanna wildlife reserve and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, home to elephants, giraffes, lions, and hundreds of bird species across open Sahelian grassland.

name: Ebolowa
description: A quiet town surrounded by dense equatorial rainforest and cocoa plantations, serving as a gateway to Cameroon's southern forest region and its biodiversity.

name: Bafoussam
description: A major highland city and cultural center of the Bamiléké people, surrounded by traditional chieftaincies ("chefferies") known for their carved architecture and royal ceremonies.

name: Reunification Monument
description: A striking spiral monument in central Yaoundé commemorating the 1961 reunification of French and British Cameroon — one of the city's most photographed landmarks.

name: National Museum of Yaoundé
description: Housed in a former presidential palace, this museum traces Cameroon's history and ethnic diversity through royal artifacts, masks, and archival photography.

name: Mvog-Betsi Zoo
description: A botanical and zoological garden on the edge of the city, home to primates, big cats, and reptiles native to Cameroon's forests, shaded by towering old-growth trees.

name: Basilica of Mary Queen of Apostles
description: A striking piece of modern religious architecture overlooking the city, also known locally as Notre-Dame des Victoires, with panoramic views from its upper level.

name: Mont Fébé
description: A hillside retreat overlooking Yaoundé, home to a Benedictine monastery and museum, and long favored for its panoramic views over the city's seven hills.

name: Mokolo Market
description: Yaoundé's largest and most vibrant market — a maze of stalls selling fresh produce, spices, fabrics, and street food, and a genuine slice of everyday city life.

name: Tchop & Yamo
description: Cameroon's first fast-food chain built around local dishes — beignets, beans, fried chicken, and fresh juices — now with branches beyond Yaoundé in Douala and Bafoussam.

name: Maison Blanche
description: A Yaoundé favorite for grilled fish and seafood — pick your catch fresh at the counter and choose how it's prepared, grilled or braised, at the Carrefour Hippodrome location.

name: Cercle Vert
description: A beloved, wallet-friendly local chain serving generous portions of grilled chicken, fufu, and eru sauce in a casual, no-frills setting.

name: Chez Wou
description: Established in 1988, this family-run restaurant is the oldest Chinese restaurant in Cameroon, now also serving local dishes alongside its original menu.
